Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G626; indefensible:--without an excuse, inexcusable.
BiblicalUsage: The word means without excuse, without defence: the invisible things of God are clearly seen from the creation of the world, so that men are without excuse — and therefore, Paul says, you are inexcusable, O man, whoever you are that judges, for in judging another you condemn yourself, because you do the same things. It appears only twice, and the second verse turns the first one on the reader.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for without excuse carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the turn — the creation leaves no one an excuse, and the judge finds he has none either.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
